# flows_project_agent_pool_attachment (Resource)

Attaches a private agent pool to a project, so that flows in the project can run on agents from that pool. Destroying the resource detaches the pool from the project; neither the project nor the agent pool is deleted.

The attachment is identified by `<project_id>/<agent_pool_id>`, which is also the ID to use when importing it. Only private agent pools of the organization can be attached: public pools are available to every project. Attaching and detaching require an API key with organization admin access, admin access to the project and the `agent_pools:edit` capability; reading the attachment only requires viewer access to the project and the `agent_pools:view` capability.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Attach a private agent pool to a project
resource "flows_project_agent_pool_attachment" "example" {
  project_id    = "your-project-id"
  agent_pool_id = "your-private-agent-pool-id"
}

# Attach the same private agent pool to several projects
locals {
  project_ids = [
    "first-project-id",
    "second-project-id",
  ]
}

resource "flows_project_agent_pool_attachment" "many" {
  for_each = toset(local.project_ids)

  project_id    = each.value
  agent_pool_id = "your-private-agent-pool-id"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `agent_pool_id` (String) ID of the private agent pool to attach.
- `project_id` (String) ID of the project to attach the agent pool to.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) ID of the attachment (composite of project_id and agent_pool_id).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import flows_project_agent_pool_attachment.example "$PROJECT_ID/$AGENT_POOL_ID"
```
